actions.action: Check under the pot for a drainage hole
Push a finger 2 inches into the soil to check moisture
Slide the plant out and inspect the roots
Trim black mushy roots and soft dark stems
Repot in fresh well-draining mix with perlite or bark in a pot with a drainage hole
Alternatively add a few inches of gravel to the bottom of the current pot
Water thoroughly only when the top 2 inches are dry and empty the saucer
Remove dead and collapsed leaves at the base
Move the plant to bright indirect light away from the hot lamp

reason: The answer names overwatering root rot as the main cause, and its unpot-and-trim fix with drainage control matches the thread's fix (soil repotting instead of water propagation is an equivalent treatment); nothing in it is likely to harm the plant.
